parsed.explanation: Combined regime imposes Tier-1 universal exposure: national binary-sex definition, passport/visa marker restrictions with discrepancy-based refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, plus division restrooms matching birth certificate enforced by ID checks and facility fines. Documented bathroom arrest, men's-ward holding, hormone removal in custody, and invasive enforcement create detention and severe custody risks if outed. Courts have enjoined some national orders and national employment/hate-crime protections exist, but state hate-crime law excludes gender identity, no statewide anti-discrimination protection applies, and remedies are slow and inconsistent. No execution or highly likely imprisonment, yet outing foreseeably leads to exclusion, humiliation, arrest risk, and misgendered custody.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport policy, X/mismatched markers stopped, Supreme Court allowed restrictions; visa cable directs refusal on discrepancy and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passports reported confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiration; civil-liberties suit challenging policy; some executive orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, secondary investigation, and later facility or custody placement by birth-certificate sex.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Bathroom trespass arrest with handcuffing and 24-hour men's-ward holding documented nationally; national corrections policies include hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Bathroom offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; pretrial release occurred in documented arrest; courts review some claims.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facility use can lead to birth-sex ward placement; division prison law covers restrooms only, not cell assignment, but national custody practices remain operative.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law effective Dec 2025 requires restrooms match birth-certificate sex in schools, universities, prisons and government buildings; $25,000/$125,000 facility fines; troopers checked ID at women's restrooms days after enactment.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trans women holding female ID were admitted in that check; exemptions exist in comparable national trespass statute; capital city council sought circumvention.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National binary definition plus division birth-certificate rule makes state ID, foreign documents, and presentation mismatch a recurring checkpoint exposure.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care banned in division since 2023; national orders target minor care, subpoenas of hospital records, and proposed bar on public insurance for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: No documented operative protection for visitor hormone continuity; several national measures blocked or in litigation, outcome uncertain.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking or medication possession can trigger investigation, disclosure, and referral into school, family-services, or law-enforcement systems.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders define sex as binary at birth, remove gender-identity materials, direct investigation/prosecution over school social transition; counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memorandum invokes 'radical gender ideology'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders enjoined; counterterrorism text says powers not for mere disagreement; marriage and employment protections remain nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing increases police, school, and border scrutiny and reduces confidence that complaints will be treated neutrally.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parental-rights law mandates deadnaming/misgendering, bans LGBT student organisations; teachers face criminal investigation for facilitating social transition; school district investigated under bathroom law; minor care banned.
minors_guardians.protection: Five district attorneys initially refused child-abuse directives and injunction blocked them; court challenges ongoing.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces school/facility exclusion and forced outing; a guardian may face investigation if care or social transition is facilitated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded killings of trans women 2008-2025, about 7.6 per 100k trans women/year, without general homicide baseline in dossier; troopers conducted restroom ID checks; state hate-crime enhancement excludes gender identity and prosecutions rare.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; protests and city council opposition documented; no documented pattern of police protection failure beyond facility enforcement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State-enforced facility checks are the clearest police-contact risk; street violence frequency cannot be assessed against background rate from dossier.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies slow, inconsistent and often ineffective: survey of custody claim failed on appeal, bathroom guidelines unclear, DOJ records demands escalated, enforcement uneven.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts enjoined some orders, allowed passport challenge litigation, recognised employment protection; legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial judicial relief does not cancel operative border, facility, school, or custody rules unless a specific order is enjoined.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine police identity checks, humiliation, fines/detention without execution and weak judicial deference. This case is similar or slightly higher risk due to statutory birth-certificate facilities rule, border fraud consequences, and custody hormone removal, but courts have enjoined some measures.

Higher risk than 0.55-C: ward/document-based placement there caused delayed or denied care without routine ID checks by troopers, criminal trespass exposure, permanent visa fraud risk, or national threat-framing guidance.

Materially lower than 0.65-A: there a brief stop ended with apology, compensation and reliable release. Here exposure is statutory and repeated across facilities, entry and custody, with no documented compensation or disciplined enforcement pattern.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction is cumulative: binary national definitions and passport/visa screening can out a visitor, division birth-certificate facility law converts that outing into exclusion or ID-check confrontation, trespass liability and custody placement create arrest and misgendered detention risk, and minor-care/school rules expose travelling families. Court injunctions, existing X validity, national employment and hate-crime protections, and admitted female-ID holders prevent a lower severe-risk rating, but they do not provide a consistent operative remedy for the documented universal exposures.
